title: Logic Apps and the integration written without code

videos.script: Every morning at six, the shop's finance team wants the orders in their inbox. Three developers could write that as a function. Or nobody writes any code. {{designer}} Logic Apps draws the job as boxes on a canvas. A clock, a call to the shop's API, a condition, an email. Under the boxes is a JSON document, and that document is the workflow. {{document}} You will write it in Bicep and compile it on your laptop. The compiler checks the resource around the workflow. Inside, it checks nothing. You will misspell a step and a function, and watch both compile clean. {{opaque}} Then connectors, the part you would otherwise write yourself. A connection to Outlook is a resource of its own, and somebody has to sign in to it. A trigger either asks on a schedule or is told. {{connectors}} Then two products under one name. Consumption bills every step it runs. Standard is an app on a plan, on the Functions runtime. {{plans}} Last, the honest comparison. When lesson 17's Durable Functions or a plain function wins, and why the morning email is better without any code. {{choice}} Nothing of Logic Apps runs on a laptop, so most of this lesson is read, and it says so each time.
